svg.title: Custom Distro component architecture
svg.desc: All 88 declared packages and 6 source projects, grouped by function from applications to the Linux kernel. Boot, development and alternate components are shown separately. See components.md for linked text equivalents.
svg.text: Component architecture · from applications to the Linux kernel
88 package recipes · 6 source projects · grouped by function
P = package recipe S = source repository Placement shows responsibility, not every dependency.
Installed desktop applications, including Telorgon SDK applications and native Wayland clients.
Screen-sharing selection UI; capture support depends on the packaged SDK capability.
The shell and applications share SDK code; the SDK is not a separate background service.
Desktop, taskbar, window management, composition and input
UI, rendering, hosting, media and service integration; also
Cooperating services and their supporting libraries, grouped by the capability they provide.
logind and user managers; D-Bus carries
Libraries and data used by the compositor and services to work with kernel devices and clients.
access and GBM buffers; the distro uses
Unicode shaping and CPU pixel composition.
libseat includes seatd; libgudev wraps the selected libudev provider for GLib clients.
Shared foundations used across the upper layers; applications can call them directly.
C and C++ runtimes, compiler support,
regular expressions, XML and PNG decoding.
Early userspace and repair tools, login and mount utilities,
The boundary between userspace and hardware, including the virtual hardware exposed by QEMU.
Scheduling, memory, filesystems, networking, drivers, DRM/KMS, input, ALSA, V4L2 and FUSE.
07 Boot handoff — before the running desktop
UEFI/OVMF → Telorgon EFI → Linux → BusyBox initramfs → root filesystem → profile-selected init.
EFI application that selects and starts the kernel and initramfs; shares boot UI code from the SDK.
08 Development, build data and alternate providers
Catalog components with special roles; these are not an additional layer below the kernel.
XML used during builds; not desktop
Catalog view: profiles select installed components; SDK features determine available capabilities.
Recipe and source manifests remain authoritative. Linked component index: docs/components.md
